name: Eczema
description: Eczema, also known as atopic dermatitis, is a common skin condition that causes the skin to become red, itchy, and inflamed. It can affect people of any age but often starts in childhood.
symptoms: Redness and itching of the skin
Skin cracking or bleeding in severe cases
risk_factors: Family history of eczema or allergies
Personal history of other allergic conditions (asthma, hay fever)

daily_routine.step: Gentle skin cleansing with lukewarm water
daily_routine.purpose: To remove dirt and excess oils without irritating the skin

daily_routine.step: Application of a fragrance-free moisturizer immediately after bathing
daily_routine.purpose: To lock in moisture and prevent dryness

natural_remedies: Applying cold compresses to soothe itchiness
Using a humidifier in dry environments
common_myths: Eczema can be 'cured' with home remedies.
when_to_consult_doctor: If symptoms persist despite self-care measures or worsen over time

severity_levels.mild: Mild eczema involves occasional itching and dryness, primarily affecting small areas of the skin.
severity_levels.moderate: Moderate eczema includes more frequent itching, redness, and dryness in larger areas of the skin.
severity_levels.severe: Severe eczema is characterized by intense itching, widespread rash, and possible complications such as infections.

expert_tips: Regular follow-ups with a dermatologist to monitor progress and adjust treatment plans
Education about eczema to better manage the condition
